en.headline: Rescuers search Kowloon Peak after climber falls
en.dek: Police were told shortly after 2:30pm that a man had fallen while climbing with a colleague near Suicide Cliff. Fire crews and a helicopter were sent.
body: Firefighters and the Government Flying Service were searching Kowloon Peak on Friday afternoon after a man was reported to have fallen while climbing.

Police received a report at about 2:30pm that two men had been climbing near the area known as Suicide Cliff when one of them fell from height, local media reported. Ming Pao said the caller told police the man was about 50 and was a colleague. Hong Kong 01 reported that he was attached to a rope.

Fire services organised teams to hike in, and the Government Flying Service sent a helicopter to search from above, according to reports from the scene. Oriental Daily said rescuers had located the man by about 4pm and were roping down to reach him. His condition had not been confirmed by police in statements carried by those outlets.

The Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department lists the Suicide Cliff area among high-risk country-park locations where fatal or serious accidents have occurred. Authorities had not stated a cause.

zh.headline: 飛鵝山攀石男墮下 消防及飛行服務隊搜救
zh.dek: 警方下午約2時半接報，一名男子與同事在自殺崖一帶攀石時墮下，救援人員正登山施救。
body: 星期五下午，一名男子在飛鵝山攀石期間墮下，消防及政府飛行服務隊到場搜救。
本地傳媒報道，警方約下午2時半接獲報案，指兩名男子在俗稱自殺崖一帶攀石，其中一人從高處墮下。《明報》引述報案人指，墮下的是約50歲男同事。香港01報道，事主身上繫有繩索。
報道指，消防派出隊伍徒步登山搜索，政府飛行服務隊亦派直升機在上空協助。《東方日報》稱，救援人員約下午4時鎖定事主位置，並以游繩施救。各報道未見警方確認其傷勢。
漁農自然護理署把自殺崖列為郊野公園曾發生致命及嚴重意外的高危地點。當局暫未公布意外原因。
